newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Sept grain contracts end quietly, meal down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Sept grain contracts end quietly, meal down.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade September grain and soybean contracts expired quietly at 1201 CDT/1701 GMT Thursday while September soymeal futures ended sharply lower in thin volume, floor traders said.
"Tenco was an outright seller of the September soymeal but it was really light volume," a floor trader said. "LIT America and Iowa Grain were spreaders."
Traders had said on Wednesday the expiry had the potential to be explosive due to high open interest levels and few deliverable stocks.
September soybeans rallied earlier in the day to $8.50 per bushel, a contract high, before falling off the highs as buying waned.
"September had a big open interest number and obviously someone was caught short," a trader said, referring to the runup early runup in September soybeans.
Open interest in September beans was 3.675 million bushels, down 2.333 million bushels from Wednesday morning.

Floor sources said Tenco Inc had purchased up to two million bushels September during the rally. Cargill Inc and Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus, were said to be sellers, traders said.
Tenco Inc also reportedly spread one million bushels Sep/Nov, traders said.
Open interest in September corn as of Thursday morning stood at 6.09 million bushels, down 9.88 million from Wednesday morning, according to CBOT data.
September corn remained in fast dealings most of the day but trading was rangebound, pit sources said.
Wheat futures were mostly quiet but fell 10-1/2 cents per bushel before noon CDT as longs liquidated, traders said.
"In wheat and corn, the shorts were worried and they got out earlier today," a trader said.
Most of the trades in corn and wheat were said to be small orders with most players rolling positions forward into deferred months, pit sources said.
Continental Grain reportedly spread 200,000 bushels Dec/Sep wheat on the day while Cargill Inc spread 200,000 Sep/Dec, traders said. Chicago Corp spread 500,000 Dec/Sep wheat, traders said.
In corn, Griffin Trading spread 500,000 bushels Dec/Sep while Tenco Inc spread 300,000 Sep/Dec, traders said.
September soybeans ended at $8.35 per bushel, up 15-1/2 cents from Wednesday's close. Soymeal ended down $8.90 per ton at $266.00 and soyoil finished at 25.18 cent a lb, up .03 from Wednesday.
Corn settled at $3.54-3/4, down 3/4 cent from Wednesday. Wheat closed at $4.22 per bushel, down 10-1/2 cents from Wednesday.
